From <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>y</mi></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = \sqrt{y} + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = y + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>y</mi></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \pi\int_0^1 \left(2\sqrt{y} - y - y^2\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \pi\left(\frac{4}{3} - \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The axis is below the region, so the far edge is the top curve: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) - (-2) = f(x) + 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Top curve minus the axis height <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Subtracting <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> adds 2.
That is measured from the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) + 2</annotation></semantics></math> is the inner radius, to the nearer curve.

why.correct: The axis is on the right, so the left curve is farther from it: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = 5 - g(y)</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: From an axis on the right, the left edge is the far edge.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 - h(y)</annotation></semantics></math> is the inner radius, to the nearer (right) curve.

That is negative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(y) < 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

The far edge gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: True: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = \sqrt{x} - (-1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 1 - (-1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

True: the axis is above, so the parabola is farther: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = 2 - x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2 - x</annotation></semantics></math>.

False: from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3</annotation></semantics></math> the far edge is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3 - \sqrt{x}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi\int_1^4 \left[2^2 - (3 - \sqrt{x})^2\right]\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

The washer's area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(R^2 - r^2) = \pi(R - r)(R + r)</annotation></semantics></math> keeps the same width <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R - r</annotation></semantics></math> but a larger <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R + r</annotation></semantics></math>, so each ring has more area.
options: Same width, larger average radius: more area per washer.
The region does not change; only the axis moves.
The hole gets larger: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> grows from 1 to 2.

The increase depends on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>: it is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi(R - r)</annotation></semantics></math>, not a fixed <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.
